items.title: Mozambique and China advance cassava value chain development
items.summary: Maputo, 30 Oct (AIM) – Mozambique and China are taking concrete steps to develop the country’s cassava value chain, aiming to boost agricultural production, promote local processing, and expand access to the Chinese market. The initiative entered a new phase following a meeting in Shenzhen, China, between Mozambique’s Chamber of Commerce (CCMI) and Chinese partners to map out the implementation of a Memorandum of Understanding signed in Maputo on 1 October. According to the independent newsheet “Integrity”, the meeting was attended by CCMI Board Chairperson Thani Cabir and CCM Executive Director Fileu Pave. The project initially targets the southern provinces of Gaza and Inhambane, focusing on cassava cultivation, processing, and commercialization. Implementation of the agreement will engage local cooperatives, business associations, and private partners, notably the Longrun Group, which is expected to facilitate technology transfer, strengthen smallholder farmer capacity, and generate local employment.

items.title: Mozambique renews Kenmare’s concession for one of world’s largest titanium mines until 2044
items.summary: The Irish mining company Kenmare Resources said in a market announcement that the Council of Ministers had approved the extension until 2044 of the rights and concessions covered by the Implementation Agreement (IA) for the Moma heavy mineral sands mine, in Nampula province, northern Mozambique. The extension includes changes to the tax, commercial and investment regimes Kenmare Resources added that approval was granted on 13 October and official notification was received by the company on 29 October The company has operated the Moma mine since 2007 and says that production from the complex accounts for around 6% of the world’s supply of titanium feedstocks, supplying customers in more than 15 countries with products used in the paint, plastics and ceramic coatings industries The IA governs the terms under which Kenmare’s subsidiary Kenmare Moma Processing (Mauritius) Limited (“KMPL”) conducts its mineral processing and export activities.

items.title: Mozambique: Banks leave benchmark lending rate unchanged at 15.5% for seventh consecutive month
items.summary: The decision follows previous ones and is in line with that of the Bank of Mozambique, which at the end of September left its MIMO benchmark policy rate unchanged at 9.25%, a level maintained since January The rate set by the AMB, known as the ‘prime rate’, has fallen progressively since January 2024, following six consecutive months at a record high of 24.1%. In January this year, the AMB cut the rate by 10 basis points to 15.7%, keeping it unchanged in February.

items.summary: Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, has been hit by a $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack Half of the assets have been frozen but many remain in the hands of the hackers, the cryptocurrency giant said Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit, though no one has claimed responsibility. items.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
items.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap.

items.title: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete who soiled herself in race tells BBC
items.summary: Australian Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk says she made the wrong decision when she continued to race after soiling herself during a competition in Beijing Speaking exclusively to the BBC, she suggested her determination to win the race in September had clouded her judgement Roughly halfway through her event last month, Wietrzyk suffered a bout of diarrhoea and images of faecal matter on parts of her body were widely shared online "I didn't really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry for everyone that I did affect," the athlete told the BBC She also talked about the effect of the social media reaction after the incident, saying she should not have received "such backlash", and that she is "only human"

items.title: Human trafficking victims stranded in Guinea-Bissau
items.summary: Dozens of West Africans lured to Guinea-Bissau with promises of jobs and migration to Europe say they were exploited by a suspected trafficking network. Now many cannot afford to return home This article contains descriptions of rape, exploitation and sexual assault. Reader discretion is advised Sadio Konimba had hoped for a better future. The 26-year-old had lost her husband and was left alone with her child in Bamako, the capital of Mali When an acquaintance told her about the possibility of reaching Europe via the West African nation of Guinea-Bissau , she decided to make the journey. She left her 6-year-old daughter behind with relatives for the time being Konimba says she was invited to the country's capital, Bissau, with the promise of work and better chances of eventually continuing on to Europe She was told the journey from Bamako to Bissau would cost between 100,000–125,000 CFA francs (roughly €150-€190, or $170-$210), which she paid.

items.title: Careless dismissals give Australia route to series win
items.summary: The winner of the third Test will finish the series top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankings Third Test, Cape Town (day three of five) South Africa 329 & 140-4: Ackerman 62; Starc 2-29 Australia 429: Inglis 102; Harmer 4-104 Batters carelessly gifting wickets to Australia... we have been here before This time it was not England helping their opponents, although they will have taken note with a tour of South Africa to come this winter South Africa's attempt to fight back in the decisive third Test against Australia was hurt by two poor strokes on day three Having taken the last six Australian wickets for 99 runs in the morning despite Josh Inglis' second Test century, the Proteas began their second innings facing a deficit of exactly 100 They needed runs from their experienced opener and number three. Neither Aiden Markram nor David Bedingham could deliver By the end, even captain Temba Bavuma had been tempted into a wild swipe to fall for 35.

items.title: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over DR Congo conflict
items.summary: Eastern DR Congo has been plagued by conflict with M23 recapturing Goma and then Bukavu in early 2025 The United States has imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its alleged support for the M23 rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing pressure on Kigali to withdraw its troops and halt support for the rebels "Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said The sanctions come months after Rwanda and DR Congo signed a US-brokered peace agreement aimed at ending the conflict Fighting has continued in eastern DR Congo since early 2025, when M23 seized the cities of Goma and Bukavu. Rwanda denies backing M23 The US Treasury says Rwanda's defence ministry directed thousands of troops to fight alongside M23 in eastern DR Congo, providing weapons, equipment, logistics and training The M23 has seized mineral-rich areas, including gold-mining sites in South Kivu and Rubaya, a major coltan-producing area in North Kivu.
